Instead of hard- coding an API endpoint directly into your agent, which would be fragile and hard to govern, the agent calls an MCP server. That server acts as a secure intermediary.

[03:03] A2A is another open protocol. This one was originally developed by Google and Microsoft supports it for multi- aent interoperability. Notice the pattern here. Open standards, multiple vendors supporting them. That's intentional. It prevents lock in. While MCP handles agentto tool communications, A2A handles agentto agent communications.

[03:33] Different problem, different protocol. A2A enables agents to communicate, delegate tasks, and collaborate across platforms. And here's where it gets powerful. Multi- aent workflows. One agent plans, another executes, and a third validates. They coordinate through A2A.

[03:58] A co-pilot studio agent can delegate a task to a foundry agent. They don't have to be on the same platform. Agents can ask for clarification or hand off complex tasks to more capable agents. For example, a research agent finds relevant documents. It hands those documents to a summarizer agent that distills the key points. That summarizer passes the results to an approver agent that validates everything before surfacing it to the user. Three agents working together, coordinated through A2A. And it works across platforms.
